scope: Completed loading, original/worker PCM, protocol, native audio, functional, browser-room and dome-motion records only; no product changes or browser execution by this summary.
scopeLimits: Each loading revision has one cold and one warm observation; no repeated timing inference.
Native low audio is a different condition from high controlled functional/readPixels tests.
Native cadence is original main-rAF callback start intervals, not presented FPS or GPU time.
Native paired live windows start at different musical times; none is eligible for strict same-time causal FPS comparison.
No physical output capture, listening test, audio underrun counter, graph CPU profile or full AudioNode count.
No physical iOS Safari/Android/desktop GPU, battery/heat or hours-long stability claim.

hall.method: One fresh Chromium launch and one explicit browser context per configuration. Cold is the first navigation; warm is a second navigation to the identical URL after about:blank in the same context, without clearing HTTP cache. No Playwright route interception or network throttling. A local proxy rewrites the document font links and exactly one solo-audience generator in main.js to seeded(417); the main fixture is fetched as identity, served as identity with its own QA ETag and no-cache, and recorded separately from original application-JS bytes. Global Math.random and Three UUID generation are unchanged. All other app JavaScript, MP3, vendor and music responses retain original gzip, ETag and cache headers. Main scene rAF is captured from the first frame, so repeated software rasterization is excluded while actual scene construction, PMREM, AudioContext/IR, full preset sample decode, applause preparation and score load run. Ready means the real solo-entry button becomes enabled, measured by MutationObserver. Crowd count and a sorted occupied-seat fingerprint must agree between cold/warm and in a separately checked baseline/candidate pair. This is controlled startup, not normal full-frame interactive readiness. Each cold/warm result is one observation, not a statistically stable benchmark.
limitations: Renderer identity is recorded in each run. Mobile is viewport/touch/UA emulation on this machine, not a real phone. A software-rendered result does not predict a physical GPU.
Cold refers to browser HTTP cache only. The upstream Node server, OS filesystem cache, local fonts and process-level startup state may already be warm.

CDP loadingFinished.encodedDataLength is the browser-reported received encoded response size; it is not exact request-upload bytes or network packet bytes. Worker subrequests may be absent from the page CDP stream; the proxy transaction log covers actual upstream requests independently.
Local controlled-font bytes are reported separately. Font timing/network behavior does not represent the external Google Fonts service.

The /js/main.js fixture response has different source bytes, identity encoding and a QA ETag. Its responseEncodedBytes and Resource Timing sizes are fixture transfer observations, not original main.js transfer bytes. Original and served identity SHA-256/byte counts are recorded per navigation.

Only the solo audience RNG is fixed. Generated room-impulse samples and other procedural random values remain native; their sample lengths and construction loops are unchanged. Occupancy equality does not prove every scene or IR byte is identical, and one observation does not establish a causal population-level timing improvement.
Heap snapshots are coarse usedJSHeapSize observations, not peak memory, audio-native memory or GPU memory measurements.

UI-ready and dome-mesh-visible are separate observations. The latter only sees mesh.visible===true, polled every 100ms, without setting visibility or rendering a frame. It is not proof of successful shader compilation, pixels displayed, or first full interactive readiness. Existing network/resource metrics are captured before awaiting this extra observation; the next warm navigation starts only after it settles.

audienceFixture.policy: Reuse fixedAudienceMain: replace exactly one solo-audience rand expression with an independent seeded generator. Global Math.random=417 and room seeding remain unchanged. Approach the chosen free seat at z+0.2 and require the real E/touch sit result to match its index.

main.meaning: This main response is a QA fixture with one isolated solo-audience seed. Its transfer bytes are not the original main.js transfer bytes. Other JavaScript, vendor, music and MP3 responses remain pass-through.

audienceFixture.responseMethod: Playwright route.fulfill of the one main.js URL; status 200, identity UTF-8, QA ETag and no-cache. This is not the loading proxy and does not measure original transfer/cache performance.

environment.commandLineError: cdpSession.send: Protocol error (Browser.getBrowserCommandLine): Command line not returned because --enable-automation not set.

audienceFingerprint.method: SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify of numerically ascending occupied indices, once after entered frame and before local viewer seating. director.occupied and audience.occupied are recorded separately.

held.meaning: Score continuations checked for original event, remaining duration, skip, velocity, start time and complete call cardinality.

noteSummary.rawEvidence: observation.notes contains each origin, original score event, actual/expected arguments and mismatch fields; observation.noteAudit contains held calls and invocation mismatches.

rawRequestAudit.method: File-only re-count of every raw observation.notes entry; no row filtered from counts. scoreMatch and raw mismatch arrays checked independently of noteSummary totals.

noteSummary.lateDefinition: Observed playNote request when < native currentTime (leadMs < 0). Not an audible-glitch count.

clock.musicElapsedInterpretation: Valid only when the same piece and transport segment span the window; inspect exclusions and states.

cadence.boundaryInterpretation: Interval statistics exclude partial start/end gaps. Those gaps and frame starts / full observed wall duration are reported separately so a stall at the end is not hidden.

sameConditionComparison.note: No detected condition changes within this run only. Pair comparison must additionally match sources, collector, device, pose, preset/DPR, initial music time, piece hash and observation duration. Metadata samples cannot rule out every transient change.

limitations: A stalled running AudioContext can be observed here, but its underlying browser/audio-device/GPU/graph cause is not established by timing correlation alone.
No physical output capture, underrun counter or audible fidelity measurement. Note requests and native clock progress do not prove glitch-free audio.
voices and voiceCreated count the engine's logical voice records, not all AudioNodes, live source nodes, render quanta, graph CPU cost or the output device's underruns.
Mobile is Chromium viewport/touch emulation, not a physical smartphone or Safari.
readPixels deliberately synchronizes WebGL and can perturb execution; READBACK=0 is a separately labelled diagnostic condition.
Runtime note hashes exclude humanization and absolute timestamps; different observation durations or seek positions may produce different hashes. Per-event score matching is checked separately.

Optional live-window cadence measures starts of the original main rAF callback while actual music runs. It is not compositor-presented FPS, pure GPU time or physical audio-output validation. The collection wrappers add observation overhead.

Live-window condition checks run at frame starts, state/visibility events and 1s metadata samples. A transient state change entirely between those observations may be missed. Eligibility within one run does not prove that two runs match.

The optional fixed-audience route controls a main.js response and may affect HTTP cache behavior; it is not a loading benchmark. Matching crowd/seat fingerprints does not prove identical audio impulse-response samples, every procedural random value or physical output quality.

browserRooms.method: Actual local browser UI in two tabs of one explicit BrowserContext. Private test room only. Native main frame callback is captured and invoked solely for two final canvas checks; UI, WebSocket and Web Audio timers run normally. Low preset, crowd/effects/broadcast off and volume zero isolate the room interface. Before clicking the real start button, the host stage is snapped to the current score roster to skip the entrance/change animation; older builds without snapRoster retain their original all-player snap. The guest uses the original room playback synchronization, and roster-aware builds verify that both actual stage rosters agree. This is functional room/UI QA, not visual-quality, FPS, sound-quality or device timing measurement. cross mode additionally uses the real venue selector, an invitation to the wrong venue, automatic venue redirect and rejoining through the invitation button.

workerPcm.method: Real Chromium dedicated module Worker and real OfflineAudioContext AudioBuffers. The production engine/loader/worker/synthesizer are imported unchanged from the local server. Each PCM channel is hashed and compared with the original synchronous synthesizer in the same browser. A second page blocks workers through Content-Security-Policy to exercise real fallback. No GPU workload, app boot, actual speaker output or device audio timing is measured. Durations are single-run diagnostic observations, not performance claims.

cases.name: audio module responses match the recorded version, including absent legacy worker modules, MIME and revalidation
sample caching and byte ranges preserve exact encoded audio bytes
create a public Hall room, host identity, seed and fresh room listing
joining the other venue returns the correct venue instead of changing rooms
a Hall guest joins with identical seed and member identity
host state and commands reach guests without changing the snapshot payload
the server rejects forged guest state, commands and host handoff
a late guest receives the complete playing snapshot and a full room rejects more members
clock ping echoes the timestamp and RoomClient maintains a finite server clock estimate
pose broadcast clamps coordinates, preserves seat zero and throttles duplicate updates
local chat is sanitized, echoed to its sender and rate limited
host handoff changes authorization and host departure restores the oldest member
RoomClient automatically rejoins after a local socket drop with preserved seed and snapshot
host socket reconnect follows the recorded identity contract and preserves authorized playback state
a private Sphere room stays out of the Hall room list and broadcasts remain isolated
empty rooms leave public listings and obey the recorded immediate-close or retained-code contract

protocol.method: Functional tests of real server.js/server/rooms.js/server/ws.js and real browser RoomClient using Node WebSocket. Temporary rooms and messages exist only in a new process bound to 127.0.0.1 on an OS-assigned port. No production host, existing server or real users are contacted. This is protocol/static-serving QA, not rendered UI, audio-device synchronization or load/performance benchmarking.
